newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes ease in Asia, Murban, Dubai premiums firm.
newsitem.headline: Crudes ease in Asia, Murban, Dubai premiums firm.

text.p: Crude oil prices eased on Monday in late Asia, weighed down by sagging ACCESS futures prices, traders said on Monday.
At 0830 GMT, January cash Brent was notionally assessed at $23.10/23.15, down five cents from late Friday U.S. levels.

In paper spreads, January Brent/Dubai was assessed at $1.97/2.03, after trading at $1.99 on Friday. January/February Dubai was assessed at 45/50 cents and February/March at 42/45 cents, both up from Friday levels. Sentiment in Dubai firmed after January Dubai traded at full month quotes plus 65 cents on Friday to a U.S. major, traders said.

In late afternoon trade, rumours of a January Murban deal at ADNOC plus 63 cents circulated the market, but could not be confirmed. On Friday, January Murban was sold twice by separate European majors at ADNOC plus 60 cents and January Lower Zakum switched hands between majors at ADNOC plus 65 cents.
Some traders expect Abu Dhabi grades to gain further momentum as more buyers need to satisfy their appetite for light crudes.
However, some cautioned the high premiums above ADNOC were making the arbitrage for substitute West African crudes workable.

In regional crudes, traders said two 200,000 cargoes of December Widuri were sold at ICP plus 38 cents and plus 40 cents to China late last week. December Ardjuna was also said traded at ICP plus 50 cents to a trader.

Trade in December Oman has yet to emerge with talks over 1997 term contracts between Asian end-users and suppliers underway, traders said. They said Thailand has agreed to buy one million barrels per quarter at MPM plus nine cents. Three South Korean end users have agreed to a price ranging from MPM plus eight to eleven cents, traders said. The 1997 Stasco term price is MPM plus 11 cents.--J.Oshima/Tokyo (03-5473-3708)
